messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: Serving runtime degradation — high error rates and container restarts in cluster us-east-1a (auto-detected). Severity: page. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, containers restarting, and increased 5xx from model serving. First alert: 2109876543. Investigate immediately. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/serving-runtime

devon: @maria you're on-call right? seeing this across multiple racks, stack traces show Xid errors. I can help with triage but need owner for handoff.

maria: I'm on it, grabbing pager. Quick summary?

devon: error rate 12% on /v1/generate endpoint for prod-serving, spike started ~2109876200. Logs show NVRM Xid 13 and container restarts, and kernel shows MLX5 timeouts. Example: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 13` then pod restart within 30s.

alex: I see repeated IB (mlx5) link down messages in /var/log/messages on node gpu-1a-5: `mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5e_close: mlx5e_disable_fail: -110` and `infiniband: mlx5_cmd: 0x1c failed -110`. Packet retransmits in perf counters up 40%.

maria: taking lead. Devon, can you run `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep serving` and check pod distribution across nodes? I want to see if restarts correlate to specific nodes.

devon: pasted output here: 
```
NAME                               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
serve-model-a-7f8b6d9c6-xy12      0/1     CrashLoop  3         2h   gpu-1a-5
serve-model-b-558bdc9d7-zr33      1/1     Running     0         5h   gpu-1a-6
serve-model-a-7f8b6d9c6-ab34      0/1     CrashLoop  2         90m  gpu-1a-7
...
```

sam: I pulled the container logs from gpu-1a-5: `Allocating tensor... cudnnConvolutionForward: CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` followed by immediate OOM-ish stack. Also seeing `failed to pull ibv_create_cq: RPC error` type messages.

maria: This smells like RDMA packet loss causing NN kernels to spin/wait and leak GPU memory or fail and cause OOMs. We should isolate nodes with IB errors and move traffic. Plan: 1) Disable cross-node KV cache and force local-only to reduce inter-node RDMA; 2) Shift traffic off suspected nodes; 3) If needed, roll to fallback model variant (smaller) in the routing layer; 4) Collect debug logs (mlx5, dmesg, nv-hostengine).

oncall: Understood. I'll start node isolation. Devon/Sam — can we cordon gpu-1a-5 and gpu-1a-7 and drain pods to other healthy nodes? Use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and `--force` if necessary. Will coordinate with k8s-bot for safe evictions.

devon: Running cordon+drain now on gpu-1a-5. `kubectl cordon gpu-1a-5` -> success. Starting drain... note: some serving pods have PDBs and may not evict immediately.

k8s-bot: Eviction plan: will try up to 3 attempts per pod respecting PDB. If unable to move, fallback routing will mark node unhealthy after 60s.

sam: While that's happening I'm enabling verbose mlx5 logging: `echo 8 > /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/log_level` and collecting `ibstatus` and `ibv_devinfo`. Pasting recent `ibv_devinfo` excerpt: 
```
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (0)
link_layer: InfiniBand
max_mtu: 4096 (4)
sm_lid: 0
port: 1: state: DOWN
```

alex: port showing DOWN is consistent. Are we seeing link flaps or sustained down? perf counters show retransmits then saturation.

maria: Good. Also tell routing to start graceful fallback to CPU-only model instances in the same region for latency-sensitive customers. Devon: can you update the route table to downgrade batch size to 1 and use fallback variant for Canary group?

devon: On it. Pushing new route config: `routes.update({model: 'serve-model-a', fallback_variant: 'serve-model-a-small', batch_size:1})` -> applied to us-east-1a, will take ~20s to propagate.

incident-bot: NOTE: Automated mitigation triggered — fallback routing applied for model serve-model-a in us-east-1a. Telemetry will reflect model variant switch.

oncall: Drain completed for gpu-1a-5 for movable pods. A few PDB-blocked pods remain pinned to that node. We're setting node to `NoSchedule` and routing will avoid it.

maria: For customer impact: approx 12% errors overall in prod for last 20m, but the error rate for few enterprise tenants hit 35% depending on which AZ they were routed to. Alerting the account teams now.

alex: I recommend we also disable cross-node KV cache in the serving config to avoid RDMA calls: `kv_cache.cross_node_enabled=false` and restart serving-router. This will increase token costs but reduce inter-node RDMA pressure.

sam: Doing that now. Restarting router processes with rolling restart. Also collecting GPU error state: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` shows a weird stuck process consuming 92% memory on gpu-1a-7 — killing it to free memory.

oncall: Killed stuck process on gpu-1a-7 -> freed ~12GB. Node memory now normal.

maria: Good. Next: we need to determine root: is it InfiniBand fabric or a driver regression? I see recent kernel/drivers updates on those nodes last week. Any quick check of package versions?

devon: Nodes gpu-1a-5 and gpu-1a-7 have mlx5 driver 5.12.1-rc2, other healthy nodes are on 5.11.8.

alex: match with change log — 5.12 introduced a bug in resource handling under heavy retransmit. We should mark driver as suspect. For now, keep affected nodes cordoned and raise a kernel rollback ticket to infra and hardware ops.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-5482 "Investigate mlx5 5.12 driver causing IB link flaps in us-east-1a". Assigned to infra-team. Priority: high.

maria: For mitigation summary: 1) cordoned problematic nodes 2) drained movable pods 3) forced fallback routing to smaller models + CPU variants 4) disabled cross-node KV cache 5) killed stuck GPU process 6) enabled verbose IB and driver logging and collected dv logs.

oncall: Are customers still impacted? Monitoring shows error rate dropped from 12% -> 3% in last 5m after fallback. Latency for fallback models up ~150ms on average.

maria: That's acceptable for mitigation. We'll keep page to infra for driver rollback and to networking to check switch-level errors (possible SFP or fabric issues) — pinging infra-net. @infra-net please triage link/SFP on Top-of-Rack switches for racks 1a-5/7.

devon: Also noting repeated `Xid 13` events correlated with pod restarts on those nodes — saving logs to /mnt/incident/2109876543/ for postmortem.

sam: Collected dmesg, nv-hostengine logs, mlx5 counters, and pcap dump on the link for 10 minutes, archived to s3://incidents/2109876543/.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: mitigation steps saved in incident runbook. Please update `incident owners` and add timeline after wrap.

maria: I'll keep the incident open and coordinate with infra and networking for full root cause. Next steps: infra to roll driver back on affected nodes, networking to validate switches, and once fabric stable, uncordon and canary pods back. I'll handle customer comms with Growth about degraded performance window.

oncall: Handoff to night oncall at 2109879000 UTC, please monitor error rates and rollback status. If error rate rises above 8% again, escalate to P1.

devon: Leaving notes in the thread and runbook: `observed_signatures: [mlx5_link_down, ib_retransmits, NVRM_Xid13, serving_oom_crashloop]`

ops-bot: Runbook checkpoint saved by maria. Estimated impact window: 00:40 UTC (ongoing).

maria: Thanks everyone. Will update when infra confirms driver rollback or fabric repair. Keep adding logs to s3 path.

alex: FYI, setting temporary alert `serving.high_oom_count` to 3/min on us-east to be more aggressive during remediation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> partial. Primary mitigation applied; awaiting infra rollback and fabric validation. Next update due 2109879900.

oncall: Handoff complete. Leaving monitoring and routing adjustments in place.

maria: 2109879902 — infra confirms they scheduled driver rollback for 2109880600. Networking swapped SFP on ToR for rack 1a-7 and saw immediate link stability improvement; retaining cordon until rollback completes.

devon: last message: saved timeline and action items to /runbooks/incidents/2109876543-timeline.md. We'll prepare a postmortem once rollback and canary uncordon succeed.
